question: The illegal regime in occupied Cyprus, a vassal of Türkiye, continues to violate the human rights and freedoms of Turkish Cypriots. The prosecution of Mustafa Hürben, who is to be tried before a military court in the occupied territories on 18 January 2024 for refusing to serve in the occupation army as a reservist, adds to a long list of acts of political persecution and intimidation against Turkish Cypriots.

The illegal regime forces Turkish Cypriots, who are legal citizens of the Republic of Cyprus, to serve in the Turkish army, initially as conscripts and later as reservists. Refusal to serve is considered desertion and carries a prison sentence. Three Turkish Cypriots, Murat Kanatlı, Halil Karapaşaoğlu and Haluk Selam Tufanl, have already taken their cases to the ECHR. In view of this: 1.
What steps could the Commission take to ensure that Turkish Cypriot citizens of the Republic of Cyprus are not forced to serve in the occupation army?
What does it plan to do to protect the rights of legal residents of the Republic of Cyprus who are living under the illegal regime of the occupied territories?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.3.2024) The Commission is aware of the case of Mustafa Hürben, who was released from prison on 25 January 2024 after having served a three-day prison sentence following his refusal to pay an 800 Turkish Lira fine (around EUR 24) for exercising the conscientious objection to military service. The Union upholds the right to conscientious objection.
Under Article 10 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the Union (‘Charter’)1, everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion, including the right to conscientious objection.

Article 9 of the European Convention of Human Rights (ECHR) also upholds the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion,2 and, through the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), the right to conscientious objection.

While the acquis, including the Charter, is suspended in the areas not under the effective control of the Government of the Republic of Cyprus,3 the ECtHR holds Türkiye, a contracting party to the ECHR, responsible for violations of the ECHR in these areas.4 The Commission regularly calls on Türkiye to respect human rights and implement ECtHR judgments.

5 Under the Aid programme for the Turkish Cypriot community,6 the European Union provides support to Turkish Cypriot civil society organisations working on human rights. Among them is the Human Rights Platform which monitors and reports on the right to conscientious objection. Further, it provides services to victims of violations and proposes legal texts to improve respect for human rights.
This entity received two Union grants totalling EUR 1,450,000 for the period October 2021 to March 2026.
